chain.note: Both trees follow the paper's route: scalar bank exchange and frames, then nested labels with L<N/2, then the bit shear and complex phase interfaces with s<Wm, then the exact deficits giving s/W<m^tau with tau=sigma=1-2^{-50}, then the two volume-normalized recurrences (O(Ve^tau) interchange, O(Vd^{lambda'}) layer), then transforms, convolution, resampling with chirp and permutation cancellation, the algorithm, exact recovery and the cost table. A also grounds the O(V) node work in stated stream primitives. B keeps the complex interface as its own step parallel to the bit interface, closer to the paper's structure. Neither chain thins or breaks.

errors.says: The Neumann evaluation's tape movement is over windows of radius about sqrt(p)·alpha and costs O(tp·sqrt(p)·alpha).
errors.paper: The window of radius ceil(sqrt(p))·alpha belongs to the S' procedure. Each E call in the Neumann evaluation uses a window of radius m=ceil(sqrt(p)/(2alpha)), and the k-1 calls total O((alpha^2+1)tp(1+sqrt(p)/alpha))=O(tp·sqrt(p)·alpha).

errors.says: Every nonzero residual of an edge contains a norm-one vector, namely a coordinate unit outside the supports involved.
errors.paper: The norm-one vector in a residual is built by tensoring chosen norm-one vectors from each factor (coordinate units outside small supports, or the generators of the lines P and Q) and placing the product in an orthogonal summand. It is generally not a coordinate unit of F^{⊗3}; for example, P⊗F⊗Q contains none.

overall.reason: Neither plan has a major error, and both reconstruct the central chain from s<Wm through s/W<m^tau to the two recurrences and the final bound essentially completely. B is slightly more complete on a few core sub-steps: the k-column tensoring P3 and the endpoint signs of the complex interface, and the definitions of nu and C_1 in the guard-width bound. A states the linear-time stream primitives that B omits, adds the absorption of alternating planes, and has no errors, while B has two minor misstatements (the Neumann window radius and 'a coordinate unit' as the norm-one vector). These slight differences point both ways.
